properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Nothing here is intent, and no option is preferred.

WHERE IT CAME FROM: art:dev-reflow2-two-agent-exercise-feedback-2026-09-29, item D12. A designer agent needed the ratio of derived to asserted facts to size storage, and wrote a ~150-line script over the export because nothing served could answer it. The root cause (fact:root-cause-no-tool-can-evaluate-reflow2s-derived-relations-because-reflow2-declares-none-of-them-2026-09-29): reflow2 declares none of its 23 derived relations. They live as imperative code across about 15 core files, and the only list is the primitives study's hand-kept derived.jsonl in another repo.

SEARCHED ACCEPTED INTENT FIRST: none answers this. The nearest are req:reflow2s-code-reasons-from-the-declared-meanings-and-every-derived-relationship-is-a-declared-rule (test 3, proposed) and req:derived-relations-and-reports-are-maintained-incrementally (proposed, gated on measurement). Both are proposed, and neither names a served read of the counts.

═══ OPTIONS ═══

(a) DECLARE, THEN EVALUATE. A derived-relation declaration served as data, per relation: its name, its formula over the declared readings, and the core function that computes it. Plus one read, e.g. `derived_report`, returning a count per relation over the current design, and optionally the tuples, bounded.
⚠️ Counter: declaring 23 formulas that stay computed by hand-written code creates a second copy of each. It stays honest only if a test checks the declaration against the code, which is test 3's own "checked against" clause.

(b) EVALUATE WITHOUT DECLARING. A read that calls the existing computations and reports their counts. The smallest step.
⚠️ Counter: the list of what to call is itself a hand-kept list inside the tool. That is the class the root cause names, moved one file over.

(c) WAIT FOR THE RULE ENGINE. Let req:derived-relations-and-reports-are-maintained-incrementally deliver counts as a by-product when the rules run in an embedded engine.
⚠️ Counter: that requirement is gated on measurement showing recomputation is the cost. It may never be built for designs of today's size, and the count is wanted now (to size storage and to track test 4's baseline).

(d) STATUS QUO: a script in the primitives repo, run against exports.
⚠️ Counter: the hub's 2026-09-22 lesson, measured. A client that re-implements reflow2's computations over the export drifts from reflow2's semantics quietly. The script re-derives 22 formulas and was never diffed against the core.

COST NOTE, a finding and not a ranking: the impact closure is the one relation whose tuples are large (118,065 directed pairs on reflow2's own design, up to 6.47 million undirected). Any option that materialises tuples needs a bound for it. Counts alone do not.
properties.name: OPEN — should reflow2 serve one read that evaluates every derived relation it computes (a count per relation, optionally the tuples), and should the relations be DECLARED as data first so that read, the checks and a later rule engine all read one list?
